definition_zh: 有帮助的；有益的；愿意帮忙的
definition_en: useful and improving a situation, or willing to help others
core_image: 递过来的手：在别人卡住的时候伸了出来
scene: 搬家那天电梯坏了，邻居二话不说来抬最重的柜子，大家都说他真是帮了大忙。Our neighbour was very helpful when we moved the heavy furniture upstairs.
sceneCN: 这里 helpful 是「愿意帮忙、帮上忙」（第 1 个义项：主动提供帮助）；邻居主动来搬家具，说明他乐于助人，帮上了实际忙。

collocations.phrase: a helpful member of the team

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「有帮助地；有益地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「有益；乐于助人」
helpful 的基础词，义为「帮助」
同根反义词，义为「无助的；无能为力的」

senses.title: Willing to help others
senses.titleCN: 乐于助人的；愿意帮忙的
senses.definition: describing a person who likes to give help to others
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人喜欢主动给别人提供帮助
senses.example: The staff were friendly and helpful during our stay.
senses.exampleCN: 我们入住期间，工作人员又友好又乐于助人。
senses.why: Help comes from the idea of lending a hand; a helpful person is one whose hand is always ready.
senses.whyCN: help 的核心是「搭把手」，helpful 形容人时，就是这只手随时准备伸出去。

senses.title: Useful and making things easier
senses.definition: useful and improving a situation or making a task easier
senses.definitionCN: 有用处、能让事情或任务变得更容易的
senses.example: This map is very helpful for finding the old streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这张地图对找那些老街道非常有帮助。
senses.why: A thing that helps is a thing that moves the task forward, so useful objects are also called helpful.
senses.whyCN: 能帮上忙的东西就是推动任务前进的东西，所以有用的物品也叫 helpful。

senses.title: Giving useful information
senses.definition: giving information or suggestions that are practical and useful
senses.definitionCN: 给出的信息或建议实用、有用
senses.example: The teacher gave some helpful tips before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前老师给了一些有用的提示。
senses.why: Advice that helps you act well is itself a form of help, so useful guidance is helpful.
senses.whyCN: 能让你把事做好的建议本身就是一种帮助，所以有用的指导叫 helpful。

intro.en: Helpful is built on the old verb help plus the adjective suffix -ful.
intro.cn: helpful 由古英语动词 help（帮助）加上形容词后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成。

items.en: The verb help comes from Old English helpan, meaning to assist or to aid.
items.cn: 动词 help 来自古英语 helpan，意为帮助、援助。

items.en: The suffix -ful comes from Old English ful, meaning full of; attached to a verb it makes an adjective.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 来自古英语 ful（充满的），加在动词后构成形容词。

items.en: In Middle English, helpful appeared meaning giving aid or assistance.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，helpful 已经出现，意为给予帮助的。

items.en: Modern English uses helpful for both people who help and things that are useful.
items.cn: 现代英语中，helpful 既形容乐于助人的人，也形容有用的东西。

items.en: The root belongs to the Germanic family; related words appear in Dutch helpen and German helfen.
items.cn: 该词根属日耳曼语族，荷兰语 helpen、德语 helfen 是同族词。

note.en: These words are close to helpful in form or meaning.
note.cn: 以下词与 helpful 形近或义近，注意区分用法。

entries.definition: without help or power to act
entries.definitionCN: 同根反义词，义为「无助的；无能为力的」

entries.definition: able to be used for a purpose; helpful in practice
entries.definitionCN: 能用于某种目的、实际上有用的

entries.definition: effective in real situations rather than in theory
entries.definitionCN: 在实际情况中有效的，而非只停留在理论

entries.definition: producing good results or good effects
entries.definitionCN: 带来好结果或好处的，较正式

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its two visible parts.
normalIntro.cn: 从可见的两个部件入手记忆 helpful。

normal.en: help + -ful = full of help
normal.cn: help（帮助）+ -ful（充满）＝「充满帮助的」，即有帮助的。

normal.en: A helpful waiter fills your cup before you ask.
normal.cn: helpful 的服务生在你开口之前就把杯子续满了——「主动充满帮助」。

normal.en: Remember the pair helpless / helpful: less help versus full of help.
normal.cn: 对照记忆 helpless（缺帮助＝无助）与 helpful（满帮助＝有益）。

normal.en: The -ful suffix also appears in careful and useful.
normal.cn: -ful 后缀同样出现在 careful（小心的）、useful（有用的）里，一套记三词。

normal.en: In a shop, the helpful staff give you helpful advice.
normal.cn: 商店里 helpful 的店员会给你 helpful 的建议——一词两义一句话装下。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that never runs out of strength to lift others.
abstract.cn: 想象一只永远有力气把别人托起来的手——这就是 helpful 的画面。

abstract.en: Imagine a backpack full of tools: every situation, it pulls out something useful.
abstract.cn: 想象一个装满工具的背包，任何情境都能掏出有用的东西——helpful 的物品感。

abstract.en: Feel the word as warmth: someone stepping forward when you are stuck.
abstract.cn: 把这个词感受成一股暖意：你卡住时有人上前一步。

examples.en: The guide gave us some helpful advice about the mountain path.
examples.cn: 向导给了我们一些关于山间小路的有用建议。

examples.en: Her helpful attitude made the new students feel welcome.
examples.cn: 她乐于助人的态度让新生感到受欢迎。

examples.en: Drinking water is helpful when you have a fever.
examples.cn: 发烧时喝水是有好处的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨偶扑」——你喊一声「嗨，偶来扑一下」，扑上来搭把手的人，正是 helpful（乐于助人的）。

root: helpful 由古英语 helpan（帮助）加形容词后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成，字面义为「充满帮助的」，引申为「有帮助的；乐于助人的」。后缀 -ful 与 full 同源，属日耳曼语族固有构词法。

sensesIntro.en: From people who help to things that help, the word covers both.
sensesIntro.cn: helpful 的义项从「乐于助人的人」扩展到「有用的物与信息」，两条线都从「帮上忙」这一核心长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out at the right moment
core.cn: 核心意象：在恰当的时刻伸出的那只手

intro.en: Helpful shows a common English pattern: verb plus -ful makes an adjective.
intro.cn: helpful 展示了英语常见构词法：动词加 -ful 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin equivalents use -ax or -ivus, but -ful itself is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语对应后缀是 -ax 或 -ivus，而 -ful 本身是日耳曼语源。

items.exampleCN: 你能帮我搬这个箱子吗？

items.meaning: full of use; serving a purpose
items.example: This app is useful for learning words.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用对学单词有用。

items.example: A baby bird is helpless without its mother.
items.exampleCN: 雏鸟没有妈妈就无法生存。

items.example: She helpfully explained the rule again.
items.exampleCN: 她热心地把规则又解释了一遍。

items.meaningCN: 派生名词：有益；乐于助人
items.example: His helpfulness is known to everyone.
items.exampleCN: 他的乐于助人人人皆知。

items.example: They sent aid to the flooded town.
items.exampleCN: 他们向被淹的城镇送去援助。

definition_en: belonging to a female person, or the object form of she
core_image: 一句称呼里指向同一位女生的手势
scene: 同学们把找到的钥匙交还给那个女生，说这是她的。The students returned the lost key to the girl and said it was her key.
sceneCN: 这里 her 是「她的」（第 1 个义项：形容词性物主代词）；her 放在名词 key 前表示归属。

forms.label: 名词性物主代词对应词

derivatives.zh: 名词性物主代词，义为「她的（东西）」
反身代词，义为「她自己」

senses.title: Belonging to a female person
senses.definition: belonging to or connected with a woman or girl already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 属于或关于前文已提到的女性
senses.example: That is her bicycle parked outside.
senses.exampleCN: 停在门外的那辆自行车是她的。
senses.why: Possessive words point ownership; her turns a person into an owner tag before a noun.
senses.whyCN: 物主词标记归属，her 把一位女性变成名词前的「所有者标签」。

senses.title: Object form of she
senses.definition: used as the object of a verb or preposition, referring to a female person
senses.definitionCN: 作动词或介词的宾语，指女性
senses.example: We met her at the station yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们昨天在车站见到了她。
senses.why: When the pronoun receives the action, English switches from she to her.
senses.whyCN: 当代词承受动作时，英语把主格 she 换成宾格 her。

intro.en: Her is one of the oldest pronoun forms in English, from the Germanic system of case endings.
intro.cn: her 是英语最古老的代词形式之一，来自日耳曼语系的格变化系统。

items.en: Old English had hire, the dative and genitive form of the feminine pronoun.
items.cn: 古英语有 hire，阴性代词的与格和属格形式。

items.en: The form goes back to Proto-Germanic *hizoi, part of the he/she/it family.
items.cn: 该形式可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *hizoi，属于 he/she/it 词族。

items.en: Middle English shortened hire to her, and the spelling settled.
items.cn: 中古英语把 hire 缩短为 her，拼写就此固定。

items.en: Modern English keeps her for both possession and object uses.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 her，兼作所有格与宾格。

items.en: The exact pre-Germanic source of the feminine pronoun stem is uncertain; forms are reconstructed.
items.cn: 阴性代词词干的前日耳曼来源不确定，形式为构拟。

note.en: These pronoun forms are easily mixed up.
note.cn: 以下代词形式极易混淆，注意格与所属关系。

normalIntro.cn: 把 her 放进 she 词族里记。

normal.en: she does, her receives, hers owns
normal.cn: she 做动作，her 承受动作，hers 表示拥有——一句话分清三格。

normal.en: her book, his book: only the middle letter changes.
normal.cn: her book 与 his book 只差中间一个字母，性别也随字母换。

normal.en: Remember hire (Old English) to see why her is short.
normal.cn: 想想古英语的 hire，就明白 her 为什么这么短。

normal.en: In We saw her, the action lands on her.
normal.cn: 在 We saw her 里，动作落在 her 身上——宾格的场景感。

normal.en: Pair it with hers: This bag is her bag; this bag is hers.
normal.cn: 对照 hers：her 后面必须跟名词，hers 单独站。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow pointing from the sentence to the girl.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭从句子射向那个女生——her 就是箭头的落点。

abstract.en: Feel her as a quiet tag that hangs on a noun or hides after a verb.
abstract.cn: 把 her 感受成挂在名词上或藏在动词后的小标签。

abstract.en: Two shapes, one person: she stands, her receives.
abstract.cn: 同一个人两个姿势：she 站着发出动作，her 接收动作。

examples.en: I borrowed her notes before the history exam.
examples.cn: 历史考试前我借了她的笔记。

examples.en: Everyone cheered when the team gave her the prize.
examples.cn: 当队伍把奖品递给她时，所有人都欢呼起来。

examples.en: Is this jacket hers or yours?
examples.cn: 这件外套是她的还是你的？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赫」——「赫然是她的名字」，一听就是 her（她的）。

root: her 来自古英语 hire，是阴性第三人称代词的与格与属格形式，属日耳曼语族固有代词系统，与 she、he 同族。阴性代词词干的更早来源不确定，为构拟形式。

sensesIntro.en: Her covers two jobs: marking possession and receiving action.
sensesIntro.cn: her 承担两项工作：名词前标所属，动词后受动作。

definition_en: in, at, or to this place or position
core_image: 原地一顿脚：就在这个位置
scene: 导游在路口停下，指着牌子说博物馆就在这里。Stop here; the museum entrance is just behind that gate.
sceneCN: 这里 here 是「在这个地方」（第 1 个义项：指当前位置）；导游示意就在此处停下。

derivatives.zh: 由 here 加 by 构成，义为「特此；以此」
由 here 加 after 构成，义为「今后；此后」

senses.title: In or at this place
senses.definition: in or at the place where the speaker is or is pointing
senses.definitionCN: 在说话者所在或所指的地方
senses.example: The keys are here on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙就在这儿桌上。
senses.why: Place words split into near and far; here is the near half, wherever the speaker stands.
senses.whyCN: 地点词分远近，here 指说话者身边的近处。

senses.title: To this place
senses.definition: to this place or position
senses.definitionCN: 朝这个地方来
senses.example: Please bring the chairs here.
senses.exampleCN: 请把椅子搬到这儿来。
senses.why: When movement ends at the speaker, here marks the destination.
senses.whyCN: 当移动以说话者为终点，here 标出目的地。

senses.title: At this point in time or speech
senses.definition: at this point in a text, activity, or process
senses.definitionCN: 在文章、活动或进程的这个节点
senses.example: Here the story takes a surprising turn.
senses.exampleCN: 故事在这里出现惊人转折。
senses.why: Spoken text also has positions; here marks the spot in it.
senses.whyCN: 口头的叙述也有「位置」，here 标出其中的节点。

intro.en: Here is an ancient place adverb, related to he and this.
intro.cn: here 是古老的地点副词，与 he、this 同出一源。

items.en: Old English hēr meant in this place.
items.cn: 古英语 hēr 意为「在这个地方」。

items.en: It goes back to Proto-Germanic *hiar, built on the hi- demonstrative stem.
items.cn: 它源自原始日耳曼语 *hiar，建立在 hi- 指示词干上。

items.en: Middle English kept her, here with the same meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 her、here，意义不变。

items.en: The spelling here became fixed, and compounds like hereby grew.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 here，并派生出 hereby 等复合词。

items.en: Some paired forms such as hither were reinforced by Norse heðan and hither.
items.cn: hither 等成对形式受到古诺斯语 heðan、hither 的强化。

note.en: Here mixes easily with sound-alikes and its opposite.
note.cn: here 易与音近词及反义词混淆。

entries.definitionCN: 「她的／她」，与 here 仅差一个字母

entries.definitionCN: 「本地的」，与周围一带相关

normalIntro.en: Keep here close to its family and opposite.
normalIntro.cn: 把 here 放进词族和反义词里记。

normal.en: here = near, there = far
normal.cn: here 近、there 远，成对记最稳。

normal.en: hear /hɪə/ and here /hɪə/ sound the same: you hear sounds here.
normal.cn: hear 与 here 同音：你在这里听见声音——一句话锁住两个词。

normal.en: Here you are is said when you hand something over.
normal.cn: 递东西时说 Here you are（给你），场景化记忆。

normal.en: From here on marks a starting point.
normal.cn: from here on（从现在起）把 here 用到时间起点上。

normal.en: Old English hēr still hides inside modern here.
normal.cn: 古英语 hēr 就藏在今天的 here 里，拼写几乎没变。

abstract.en: Stamp your foot once: the spot under your shoe is here.
abstract.cn: 原地跺一下脚：鞋下的那块地方就是 here。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight fixed on one tile of the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯固定在地板的一块砖上——here 的位置感。

abstract.en: Feel here as a small flag the speaker plants.
abstract.cn: 把 here 感受成说话者插下的一面小旗。

examples.en: Come here and look at this photo of the old bridge.
examples.cn: 过来一下，看看这张老桥的照片。

examples.en: The bus stops here, not at the next corner.
examples.cn: 公共汽车在这里停，不在下一个街角。

examples.en: Here the recipe needs two eggs, not three.
examples.cn: 食谱在这里需要两个鸡蛋，不是三个。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿儿」——喊一声「嘿儿，过来」，人就到了 here（这里）。

senses.title: A person admired for great courage
senses.definition: a person admired for brave or noble deeds, especially in danger
senses.definitionCN: 因勇敢或高尚的行为而受敬仰的人，尤指临危之时
senses.example: Firefighters are often called heroes.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员常被称为英雄。
senses.why: Great courage sets a person apart, and the crowd names that person a hero.
senses.whyCN: 非凡的勇气使人出类拔萃，众人便称其为英雄。

senses.title: The main male character in a story
senses.definition: the main male character in a novel, film, or story
senses.definitionCN: 小说、电影或故事中的男主角
senses.example: The hero finally defeats the villain in the last chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 男主角在最后一章终于击败了反派。
senses.why: Stories centre on one strong figure; the old word for that figure is hero.
senses.whyCN: 故事围绕一个强力人物展开，这个人物的老称呼就是 hero。

senses.title: Someone greatly admired in a field
senses.definition: a person admired for a special skill or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因特殊才能或成就而受崇拜的人
senses.example: Young players treat the former champion as their hero.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻球员把那位前冠军当作偶像。
senses.why: Skill at a level others dream of earns the same awe as courage.
senses.whyCN: 达到他人梦想级别的技艺，会赢得与勇气同等的崇拜。

intro.en: Hero travelled from Greek myth into Latin, French, and finally English.
intro.cn: hero 从希腊神话出发，经拉丁语、法语传入英语。

items.en: Greek hērōs meant a protector or defender, later a demigod honoured after death.
items.cn: 希腊语 hērōs 意为保护者、守护者，后指死后受尊崇的半神。

items.en: Latin borrowed heros for legendary men of great courage.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 heros，指传奇中的勇者。

items.en: Old French heros carried the word into medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 heros 把这个词带入中世纪欧洲。

items.en: Middle English hero(e) first meant men of superhuman strength in romances.
items.cn: 中古英语 hero(e) 最初指骑士文学里具有超人力量的人物。

items.en: Modern English widened hero to war heroes, story leads, and idols.
items.cn: 现代英语把 hero 扩展到战争英雄、故事主角和偶像。

note.en: These words share roots or meanings with hero.
note.cn: 以下词与 hero 同根或义近。

entries.definition: adjective meaning very brave or grand
entries.definitionCN: 派生形容词，义为「英勇的；壮烈的」
阴性名词，义为「女英雄；女主角」

entries.definition: the quality of being a hero
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「英雄气概」

entries.definition: a person who fights or wins for others
entries.definitionCN: 为他人而战或取胜的人，义近「斗士；冠军」
受粉丝崇拜的人，义为「偶像」

entries.definition: a very famous and admired person
entries.definitionCN: 广受赞誉的名人，义为「传奇人物」

normalIntro.en: Use the Greek root and the word family.
normalIntro.cn: 用希腊词根和词族记忆 hero。

normal.en: Greek hērōs = protector: a hero protects others.
normal.cn: 希腊语 hērōs 意为「保护者」：英雄就是保护他人的人。

normal.en: hero + -ic = heroic; hero + -ism = heroism.
normal.cn: hero 加 -ic 成 heroic（英勇的），加 -ism 成 heroism（英雄气概）。

normal.en: The plural needs -es: one hero, two heroes.
normal.cn: 复数要加 -es：一个 hero，两个 heroes。

normal.en: heroine is the female hero, with -ine like in Josephine.
normal.cn: heroine 是女英雄，-ine 如人名 Josephine 中的阴性后缀。

normal.en: A hero sandwich is hero in name only.
normal.cn: hero sandwich（大号三明治）只是借用 hero 之名，与英雄无关。

abstract.en: Picture a figure standing on a wall between the storm and the crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在墙上，挡在风暴与人群之间——hero 的剪影。

abstract.en: Hear the crowd roar one name: that name is the hero.
abstract.cn: 听见人群齐吼一个名字——那就是 hero 的声音。

abstract.en: Feel hero as a spotlight aimed at one brave silhouette.
abstract.cn: 把 hero 感受成打在一个勇敢剪影上的追光。

examples.en: The doctor worked heroically through the night to save the injured.
examples.cn: 医生英勇地通宵救治伤员。

examples.en: My grandmother is my hero; she raised five children alone.
examples.cn: 祖母是我的英雄，她独自抚养了五个孩子。

examples.en: In the film, the hero must choose between love and duty.
examples.cn: 在电影里，男主角必须在爱与责任之间做出选择。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑柚」——「黑夜里抱着大柚子救人的人」，像 hero（英雄）。

root: hero 源自希腊语 hērōs（保护者；半神），经拉丁语 heros、古法语 heros 进入中古英语。词根的更早来源不确定，一般认为与「守护、护卫」观念相关。

sensesIntro.cn: hero 的义项从战场勇气扩展到故事主角与崇拜偶像，核心始终是「被人仰望的人」。

core.cn: 核心意象：艰难时刻站在人群之上的那个人

intro.cn: hero 带动一个以希腊语源后缀构成的词族。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 heros 保留同一词干，罗曼语族有 heroe 形式。

items.example: The valiant knight held the gate.

definition_en: the one or ones belonging to a female person already mentioned
core_image: 物归其主：东西指回那位女生
scene: 两把伞长得很像，妹妹指了指门边说那把是她的。Both umbrellas look alike, but the one by the door is hers.
sceneCN: 这里 hers 是「她的（东西）」（第 1 个义项：名词性物主代词）；hers 单独作表语，后面不再接名词。

forms.label: 形容词性物主代词对应词

senses.title: Something belonging to her
senses.definition: the thing or things that belong to a particular woman or girl
senses.definitionCN: 属于某位女性的人或物
senses.example: This laptop is hers, not mine.
senses.exampleCN: 这台笔记本电脑是她的，不是我的。
senses.why: English adds -s to her so the possessive can stand alone without a noun.
senses.whyCN: 英语在 her 后加 -s，让所有格脱离名词单独站立。

senses.title: Of hers: among the things she owns
senses.definition: used after a noun to mean one of the things she owns
senses.definitionCN: 接在名词后，表示她拥有的同类之一
senses.example: A cousin of hers lives in Chengdu.
senses.exampleCN: 她的一个表亲住在成都。
senses.why: The double possessive of hers picks one item out of her whole set.
senses.whyCN: 双重所有格 of hers 从她拥有的一整类中挑出一个。

intro.en: Hers is her plus the adverbial genitive -s that English added to possessives.
intro.cn: hers 是 her 加上英语给所有格添加的副词性属格 -s 构成的。

items.en: Old English hire marked both dative and genitive of the feminine pronoun.
items.cn: 古英语 hire 兼表阴性代词的与格与属格。

items.en: Middle English added the -s ending, giving hers as a standalone possessive.
items.cn: 中古英语加上 -s 词尾，产生可独立使用的 hers。

items.en: The -s genitive follows the Germanic habit of marking possession with -s.
items.cn: -s 属格沿袭日耳曼语用 -s 标记所属的习惯。

items.en: Modern English keeps hers only as the pronoun form; her stays before nouns.
items.cn: 现代英语中 hers 只作代词，her 保持在名词前。

items.en: The older stem of the feminine pronoun remains uncertain; it is reconstructed.
items.cn: 阴性代词的更早词干不确定，为构拟形式。

note.en: Compare hers with the rest of the she-family.
note.cn: 把 hers 与 she 词族的其他形式对照。

normalIntro.en: Fix the difference between her and hers.
normalIntro.cn: 重点区分 her 与 hers 的用法。

normal.en: her + noun; hers alone: her coat, the coat is hers.
normal.cn: her 后接名词，hers 单独站：her coat / the coat is hers。

normal.en: The -s in hers means ownership without a word after.
normal.cn: hers 的 -s 表示「后面不用再跟名词」的拥有。

normal.en: a friend of hers = one of her friends.
normal.cn: a friend of hers 等于 one of her friends——双重所有格。

normal.en: Compare: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.
normal.cn: 成串记独立所有格：mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs。

normal.en: Hers is written without an apostrophe.
normal.cn: hers 拼写没有撇号，别写成 her's。

abstract.en: Picture the bag floating back to its owner with a small tag reading hers.
abstract.cn: 想象包自己飘回主人身边，挂着写着 hers 的小标签。

abstract.en: See two boxes side by side; one silently points to the girl.
abstract.cn: 两只盒子并排放，其中一只无声地指向那位女生。

abstract.en: Feel hers as a magnet that pulls the thing to its owner.
abstract.cn: 把 hers 感受成把物品吸回主人的磁铁。

examples.en: Whose phone is this? It is hers.
examples.cn: 这是谁的手机？是她的。

examples.en: She compared her results with hers from last year.
examples.cn: 她把自己的成绩与去年（那份）比较。

examples.en: That red car in the yard is hers.
examples.cn: 院子里那辆红车是她的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赫斯」——「赫然写着斯人所有」，属于她的东西就是 hers。

root: hers 由古英语 hire（阴性代词与格/属格）在中古英语时期加属格词尾 -s 而成，-s 属格是日耳曼语族的固有标记。阴性代词词干的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Hers only does one job: to own things without naming them.
sensesIntro.cn: hers 只做一件事：不点名地表示「她的东西」，两种用法都围绕独立所有格。

definition_en: the reflexive form of she, used when the object is the same female person as the subject
core_image: 动作绕一圈回到她自己的手上
scene: 妹妹坚持不用帮忙，独自把散落的拼图一块块拼好，晚饭前完成了整幅作品。The little girl completed the big puzzle all by herself before dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 herself 是「她自己；她亲自」（第 1 个义项：反身用法）；拼图由她独立完成，动作回到自身。

senses.title: Reflexive: object equals subject
senses.definition: used when the female subject and the object of the verb are the same person
senses.definitionCN: 主语与宾语为同一位女性时使用
senses.example: She looked at herself in the old mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 她照了照那面旧镜子。
senses.why: The action bends back onto the doer, so the word mirrors she.
senses.whyCN: 动作弯回施动者本人，所以这个词是 she 的「镜子」。

senses.title: Emphatic: she did it personally
senses.definition: used to stress that the female person did it personally
senses.definitionCN: 强调某事由她本人亲自完成
senses.example: The head teacher herself welcomed the new pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 校长亲自迎接了新生。
senses.why: Putting herself next to the noun singles that person out.
senses.whyCN: 把 herself 放在名词旁就把这个人单独点亮。

intro.en: Herself compounds her with the old word self.
intro.cn: herself 由 her 与古老的 self 复合而成。

items.en: Old English used hire selfum, meaning to her own self.
items.cn: 古英语有 hire selfum，意为「对她自己」。

items.en: The element self long expressed one's own person in Germanic.
items.cn: self 元素在日耳曼语中长期表「自身」。

items.en: Middle English fused the pair into the single form herself.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者融合为 herself 一词。

items.en: Modern English keeps both reflexive and emphatic uses.
items.cn: 现代英语兼有反身与强调两种用法。

items.en: The reflexive family grew in parallel: myself, himself, themselves.
items.cn: 反身代词家族同步壮大：myself、himself、themselves。

note.en: Compare herself with the reflexive family.
note.cn: 把 herself 与反身代词家族对照。

abstract.cn: 感受镜子：做者与受者是同一人。

abstract.en: See a spotlight jump onto her when herself appears.

examples.en: Mary herself will host the class meeting.

definition_zh: 嘿；喂（用于引起注意或打招呼）
definition_en: used to call attention or to greet someone informally
core_image: 隔着人群喊出的那一声招呼
scene: 操场上球飞出界外，同学们齐声喊住捡球的男孩，让他别走远。Hey, come back! The ball rolled this way, not that way.
sceneCN: 这里 hey 是「引起注意」（第 1 个义项：呼唤提醒）；同学们喊住男孩，让他注意球滚来的方向。

senses.title: To call attention
senses.definition: used to make someone notice you or something
senses.definitionCN: 用来让某人注意你或某件事
senses.example: Hey, you dropped your wallet on the floor!
senses.exampleCN: 嘿，你的钱包掉在地上了！
senses.why: A shout must be short and loud; hey is the shortest way to grab an ear.
senses.whyCN: 呼喊必须短促有力，hey 是抓住耳朵的最短方式。

senses.title: An informal greeting
senses.definition: used as a friendly, casual hello between people
senses.definitionCN: 熟人之间随口友好的问候
senses.example: Hey, long time no see! How have you been?
senses.exampleCN: 嗨，好久不见！最近怎么样？
senses.why: The same shout softens into a greeting when the meeting is friendly.
senses.whyCN: 同样的喊声在友好相遇时软化为问候。

senses.title: To show surprise or protest
senses.definition: used to show that you are surprised or annoyed
senses.definitionCN: 表示惊讶或轻微抗议的语气词
senses.example: Hey! That is my seat, not yours.
senses.exampleCN: 嘿！那是我的座位，不是你的。
senses.why: A shout that grabs attention also marks boundaries when something is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 引起注意的喊声在不对劲时也能标出界限。

intro.en: Hey is one of the oldest natural cries in English.
intro.cn: hey 是英语中最古老的天然呼喊声之一。

items.en: Middle English spelled it hei, hai, hey, used to call attention.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 hei、hai、hey，用于呼唤注意。

items.en: The Middle English cry probably echoes Old French haï, itself a call.
items.cn: 中古英语的呼喊可能呼应古法语 haï，本身也是一种呼唤。

items.en: Similar cries appear across Germanic languages, such as German hei.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语言都有类似呼喊，如德语 hei。

items.en: American English made hey a common casual greeting in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪美国英语让 hey 成为常见的随口问候。

items.en: Because it imitates a natural shout, the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 由于它模仿天然喊声，更深的来源不确定。

note.en: Compare hey with other greeting shouts.
note.cn: 把 hey 与其他招呼声对照。

definition_zh: 隐藏；把……藏起来；隐瞒；躲藏
definition_en: to put something where it cannot be seen, or to keep a fact secret
core_image: 把东西塞进看不见的角落
scene: 考试前弟弟把漫画书压在枕头下，怕被妈妈收走。He decided to hide the comic book under his pillow before his mother came in.
sceneCN: 这里 hide 是「藏起来」（第 1 个义项：放置使不被看见）；弟弟把漫画书压在枕头下不让妈妈发现。

senses.title: To put out of sight
senses.definition: to put something in a place where it cannot be seen or found
senses.definitionCN: 把东西放到看不见或找不到的地方
senses.example: The cat hid her toys under the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 猫把玩具藏在沙发下面。
senses.why: Out of sight means out of reach; hiding moves a thing beyond the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 看不见就够不着；藏就是把东西移出视线之外。

senses.title: To keep a fact secret
senses.definition: to keep information or feelings secret from others
senses.definitionCN: 不让别人知道某信息或某情感
senses.example: She tried to hide her disappointment about the result.
senses.exampleCN: 她尽量掩饰对结果的失望。
senses.why: Feelings and facts can be put out of sight exactly like objects.
senses.whyCN: 情感与事实可以像物品一样被移出视线。

senses.title: To go where one cannot be seen
senses.definition: to go to or stay in a place where you cannot be seen
senses.definitionCN: 到看不见自己的地方去或待在那里
senses.example: The rabbit hid in the tall grass until the hawk left.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子在高草里躲到老鹰飞走。
senses.why: A person hiding puts the body itself out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 藏起来的人把自己整个移出视线。

intro.en: Hide comes from an old Germanic root about covering and watching over.
intro.cn: hide 来自一个表示「遮盖、看护」的古日耳曼词根。

items.en: Old English hydan meant to conceal or to cover.
items.cn: 古英语 hydan 意为隐藏、遮盖。

items.en: It goes back to Proto-Germanic *hudjan, related to hud (cover).
items.cn: 它可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *hudjan，与 hud（盖）相关。

items.en: The same root gave hut, the protective covering of a body.
items.cn: 同一词根衍生出 hut，指身体的保护覆盖物。

items.en: Middle English kept hiden with both object and body senses.
items.cn: 中古英语 hiden 兼有藏物与藏身之义。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of hiding facts and feelings.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了隐瞒事实与情感之义。

examples.cn: 孩子们在花园里玩捉迷藏。

definition_zh: 高的；高处的；（数量、程度）高的；高级的

senses.title: Measuring far from bottom to top
senses.definition: measuring a long distance from the bottom to the top
senses.definitionCN: 从底到顶距离很长
senses.example: The kite flew high above the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 风筝飞到比树还高的地方。
senses.why: Upward distance is the most visible measure, so height comes first.
senses.whyCN: 向上的距离最直观，所以「高」首先指这个。

senses.title: Great in amount or degree
senses.definition: great in number, level, or intensity

senses.example: The river reached a high level after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨过后河水涨到很高的水位。
senses.why: A scale that points upward also measures amounts and degrees.
senses.whyCN: 向上的刻度同样可以度量数量与程度。

senses.title: Important or senior in rank
senses.definition: important or senior in position or rank
senses.definitionCN: 地位或级别上重要的
senses.example: She holds a high position in the company.
senses.exampleCN: 她在公司担任高级职位。
senses.why: Rank is drawn as a ladder, so seniority sits high on it.
senses.whyCN: 级别被画成梯子，资历高就站在梯子上端。

senses.title: At a strong or excited state
senses.definition: showing strong excitement or energy
senses.definitionCN: 表现出强烈的兴奋或干劲
senses.example: The fans were in high spirits after the victory.
senses.exampleCN: 胜利之后球迷们情绪高涨。
senses.why: Emotions also climb an inner scale, and excitement sits at the top.
senses.whyCN: 情绪也有内在刻度，兴奋处在顶端。

definition_en: a raised area of land that is lower and smaller than a mountain
core_image: 地面鼓起的一个平缓的包

senses.title: A small raised area of land
senses.definition: an area of land that rises above the land around it, smaller than a mountain

senses.title: A slope on a road or path
senses.definition: a slope on a road or path that goes up or down

senses.example: The bus slowed down on the steep hill.
senses.exampleCN: 公共汽车在陡坡上减速了。
senses.why: Any raised ground makes a slope for those who walk or drive it.
senses.whyCN: 凸起的地面对行人车辆来说就是坡。

intro.en: Hill is a native Germanic landscape word.
intro.cn: hill 是日耳曼语族固有的地貌词。

items.en: Old English hyll meant a hill or a slope.
items.cn: 古英语 hyll 意为山丘或坡地。

items.en: It goes back to Proto-Germanic *hulnis, related to covering and heaping.
items.cn: 它可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *hulnis，与遮盖、堆积相关。

items.en: Old Norse hallr, a stone or slope, influenced some forms.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hallr（石、坡）影响了部分形式。

items.en: Middle English kept hill as settlements spread into hill country.
items.cn: 中古英语 hill 随聚落扩展进入丘陵地带而普及。

items.en: Modern English compounds like hillside and hilltop grew common.
items.cn: 现代英语中 hillside、hilltop 等复合词流行起来。

note.en: Compare hill with mountain words.

abstract.en: See wind combing the grass on a round hill.

examples.cn: 骑车爬这个坡大约要十分钟。

examples.en: From the hill we could see the whole valley.

definition_zh: 历史学家；史学研究者；编史者
definition_en: a person who studies and writes about the past, especially by examining evidence
core_image: 一张堆满手稿的长桌，学者戴着薄手套比对两封字迹不同的信
scene: 为了弄清末代码头的归属，一位研究者花了十年翻阅港口账簿与地图，被同行称为严谨的历史学家。To settle who owned the old wharf, one researcher spent ten years reading port ledgers and maps, and colleagues called her a rigorous historian.
sceneCN: 这里 historian 指「以史料研究并书写过去的专业人员」（第 1 个义项：专业史学研究者）；句意为为了弄清末代码头归属，一位研究者花十年翻阅港口账簿与地图，被同行称为严谨的历史学家。可辨识物件：手稿长桌、薄手套、两封信、港口地图。

senses.title: A professional student of the past
senses.definition: a scholar trained to find, check and interpret evidence about past events
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、能查找、核验并解释过去事件证据的学者
senses.example: The historian spent a decade in the port ledgers before writing a single chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史学家在港口账簿里花了十年，才写下一章。
senses.why: the -ian ending marks a practitioner, so historian is the person behind the discipline of history.
senses.whyCN: -ian 词尾标记从业者，因此 historian 就是历史学科背后的人。

senses.title: A writer of narrative history
senses.definition: an author who turns evidence into a readable account for a general audience
senses.definitionCN: 把证据变成公众可读叙述的作者
senses.example: As a historian she writes for readers who have never opened an archive.
senses.exampleCN: 作为历史写作者，她为从未进过档案馆的读者写作。
senses.why: history once meant story, so the person who shapes the narrative keeps the older role.
senses.whyCN: history 曾经意为故事，因此把材料塑造成叙述的人延续了更古老的角色。

senses.title: An archival researcher
senses.definition: a specialist who works mainly on documents, registers and provenance rather than on broad narrative
senses.definitionCN: 主要处理文书、登记册与来源考证，而非宏大叙述的专家
senses.example: The provenance of the painting was settled by a historian of tax records.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画的来历由一位研究税收档案的历史学家厘清。
senses.why: the discipline's authority rests on evidence, so one identity of the historian is the person who follows paper trails.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科权威来自证据，因此历史学家的一重身份就是顺着纸面线索追查的人。

senses.title: An official or court chronicler
senses.definition: a person appointed to record events for a ruler, a city or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 受命为统治者、城市或机构记录事件的人
senses.example: The court historian recorded the campaign in a tone the general approved.
senses.exampleCN: 宫廷史官以一种将军认可的语调记录了这场战役。
senses.why: the office predates the modern profession, and appointment shaped what could be written.
senses.whyCN: 这一职位早于现代专业，任命本身决定了什么可以写。

senses.title: A historian of one field
senses.definition: a specialist in the past of a particular subject, such as science, art or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定主题（如科学、艺术或医学）之过去的专家
senses.example: A historian of medicine traced the shift from bleeding to transfusion.
senses.exampleCN: 一位医学史学家梳理了从放血到输血的转变。
senses.why: as disciplines multiplied, each needed its own reader of its records, so the word took a field complement.
senses.whyCN: 学科不断增多，每一门都需要自己的档案解读者，于是这个词带上了领域补语。

senses.title: An institutional historian
senses.definition: a person who writes the history of a company, a school or a regiment, often from internal files
senses.definitionCN: 依据内部档案撰写公司、学校或团队历史的人
senses.example: The firm's historian was given the whole correspondence of its founders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的史学家获准查阅创始人的全部通信。
senses.why: institutions need a usable past, so they hire someone to turn their files into a lineage.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个可用的过去，于是雇人把档案变成一条传承线。

senses.title: An amateur or local historian
senses.definition: a non-professional who documents the past of a place or a family with care but without formal training
senses.definitionCN: 非专业者，认真记录某地或某家族过去，但未受正式训练
senses.example: A local historian mapped every well that had disappeared from the village.
senses.exampleCN: 一位地方史研究者标出了村里每一口消失的水井。
senses.why: the role is defined by the subject and the care, not by a degree, so the word admits amateurs.
senses.whyCN: 这一角色由主题与用心程度界定，而非由学位界定，因此也容纳业余者。

senses.title: Abstract: anyone who explains the past
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何解释过去的人
senses.definition: loosely, anyone who offers an account of how something came to be
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛地指任何讲述某事物如何形成的人
senses.example: Every family has its own historian, usually the one who keeps the photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 每个家庭都有自己的史学家，通常是保存照片的那位。
senses.why: the abstract use keeps only the act of accounting for the past, dropping the archive and the degree.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法只保留「为过去作说明」这一动作，去掉档案与学位。

intro.en: Historian is history plus the person-ending -ian, modelled on French historien. The root goes back to Greek histor 'witness, one who knows'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: historian 是 history 加表示人的词尾 -ian，仿法语 historien 构成。词根可追溯到希腊 histor「见证人、知情者」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Histor meant 'witness, one who knows', generally linked to the root for seeing that also underlies English wit.
items.cn: histor 意为「见证人、知情者」，一般与表示「看见」的词根相联系，英语 wit 亦出此根。

items.en: Historia was inquiry and the knowledge gained by it, the title word of early prose research.
items.cn: historia 是探究及由此获得的知识，是早期散文研究的标题词。

items.en: Latin kept historia for both the inquiry and the written account, and the account sense became dominant.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 historia 兼指探究与成文记述，后来记述义占主导。

items.en: French formed historien for the person, adding the agent ending to the noun; English borrowed the pattern in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语在名词上加施事词尾，构成指人的 historien；英语于 16 世纪借用这一构词模式。

items.en: Historian first meant a writer of histories, and only later a salaried academic researcher with methods and archives.
items.cn: historian 最初指写史之人，后来才指领取薪俸、有方法与档案的学院研究者。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation of historian is not firmly fixed, and the pre-Greek history of histor is unsettled, so any reconstructed root is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：historian 在英语中的最早书证并不确定；histor 在希腊语之前的历史亦未定，任何重构词根都是假说。

note.en: Group one holds the adjective and root forms most often confused with the person; group two holds neighbouring keepers of the past.
note.cn: 第一组是常与「人」混淆的形容词与同根形式；第二组是相邻的「过去守护者」。

entries.definition: Describes an event important enough to be remembered; it is not the person who studies events.
entries.definitionCN: 形容重要到值得被记住的事件；不是研究事件的人。

entries.definition: Describes anything connected with the past or with the discipline; the person form is historian.
entries.definitionCN: 形容与过去或该学科有关的任何事物；指人的形式是 historian。

entries.definition: The record, discipline or account itself; historian is the practitioner of that field.
entries.definitionCN: 指记录、学科或叙述本身；historian 是该领域的从业者。

entries.definition: The analysis of how histories are written; a historian may practise historiography, but the words are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 对历史如何被书写的分析；历史学家可以从事编史学研究，但两词不可互换。

entries.definition: One who writes a chronicle, an event-by-event record; the role is closer to listing than to interpreting.
entries.definitionCN: 写编年史的人，逐事记录；其角色更接近罗列而非解释。

entries.definition: A formal title for an appointed writer of history, especially of a state or institution.
entries.definitionCN: 受任撰写历史者的正式头衔，尤指国家或机构的史官。

entries.definition: A person who preserves and catalogues documents; the archivist keeps the evidence a historian reads.
entries.definitionCN: 保存并编目文书的人；档案员保管历史学家所读的证据。

entries.definition: An older word for one who studies ancient objects and records, often as a collector rather than an analyst.
entries.definitionCN: 旧称，指研究古物与古记录的人，常是收藏者而非分析者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: history plus -ian makes the person, as music makes musician and politics makes politician.
normal.cn: history 加 -ian 构成指人的词，正如 music 构成 musician、politics 构成 politician。

normal.en: The root histor means witness, the one who was there and can tell.
normal.cn: 词根 histor 意为见证人，即在场并能讲述的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the specialisms: military historian, art historian, historian of science.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出专长：军事史学家、艺术史学家、科学史学家。

normal.en: The adjective historic means momentous; historical means relating to the past.
normal.cn: 形容词 historic 指重大，historical 指与过去有关。

normal.en: An archivist keeps the papers; a historian reads them and argues.
normal.cn: 档案员保管纸页，历史学家阅读并论证。

abstract.en: Picture thin gloves lifting two letters written in different hands.
abstract.cn: 想象薄手套捧起两封字迹不同的信。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger trail that leads from a tax entry to a whole family.
abstract.cn: 想象一条账簿线索，从一条税目通向一整个家族。

abstract.en: Picture a family album kept by the one person who remembers every name.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家庭相册，由一个记得所有名字的人保管。

examples.en: Historians disagree about the cause of the fire, though they share the same files.
examples.cn: 历史学家对这场火灾的成因意见不一，尽管他们看的是同一批档案。

examples.en: A military historian reconstructed the march from supply receipts.
examples.cn: 一位军事史学家依据补给收据重建了这次行军。

examples.en: The local historian found the well under a car park.
examples.cn: 地方史研究者在停车场下找到了那口井。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one person from the professional scholar to the narrative writer, the archive specialist, the official chronicler, the field specialist, the institutional and amateur worker, and finally anyone who explains a past.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种人展开：专业学者、叙事作者、档案考证者、官方史官、领域专家、机构史撰写者与业余研究者，最后是任何解释过去的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table of manuscripts and a pair of gloved hands comparing two letters.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张手稿长桌，戴手套的双手比对两封信。

branches.en: TRAINED READER: the professional identity rests on handling evidence correctly.
branches.cn: 受过训练的读者：专业身份建立在正确处置证据之上。

branches.en: STORYTELLER: the narrative role keeps the oldest sense of history as story.
branches.cn: 讲故事的人：叙事角色保留了 history 作为故事的最早义项。

branches.en: APPOINTED VOICE: rulers and institutions need a past written in their own files.
branches.cn: 受命发声：统治者与机构需要一段依自家档案写成的过去。

branches.en: FIELD SPECIALIST: every discipline trains its own reader of its records.
branches.cn: 领域专家：每门学科都训练自己的档案解读者。

branches.en: CARE WITHOUT A DEGREE: the role finally opens to anyone who keeps and explains the past.
branches.cn: 无关学位的用心：这一角色最终向任何守护并解释过去的人开放。

intro.en: Historian is a transparent construction: a Greek-derived noun plus the Latin-derived person ending -ian, the same ending as in musician.
intro.cn: historian 的结构很透明：希腊来源名词加拉丁来源的表人词尾 -ian，与 musician 中的词尾相同。

latinIntro.en: Latin historia builds history and historiography; the ending -ianus, through French -ien, gives the English person suffix -ian.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 historia 构成 history 与 historiography；拉丁词尾 -ianus 经法语 -ien 给出英语表人词尾 -ian。

senses.title: Relating to history
senses.titleCN: 历史的：与历史这门学问有关
senses.definition: relating to history as a field of study or to the study of past events
senses.definitionCN: 与作为研究领域的历史，或与对过去事件的研究有关
senses.example: The department publishes work on historical method.
senses.exampleCN: 该系发表关于历史方法的成果。
senses.why: history comes from Greek historia 'inquiry'; historical marks what belongs to that inquiry rather than to the present.
senses.whyCN: history 出自希腊 historia“探究”；historical 标记属于这一探究、而非当下的事物。

senses.title: Set in a past period
senses.titleCN: 历史题材的：以某一过去时期为背景
senses.definition: of a novel, film or exhibition, set in an earlier period and built from its details
senses.definitionCN: 指小说、影片或展览以较早时期为背景，并依其细节构建
senses.example: The museum's historical reconstruction shows a street of nineteen-twenties shops.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的历史复原展示了一条二十世纪二十年代的店铺街。
senses.why: A period setting borrows the record for atmosphere, so the adjective distinguishes it from stories set today.
senses.whyCN: 时期设定借用历史记录来营造氛围，这个形容词因此把它与以当代为背景的故事区分开。

senses.title: Real in the past
senses.titleCN: 历史上真实存在的：确有其人与其事
senses.definition: existing or happening in the real past rather than being invented
senses.definitionCN: 在真实的过去存在或发生，而非虚构
senses.example: The character is historical; the love affair is invented.
senses.exampleCN: 这个人物是历史上真实存在的，那段恋情则是虚构的。
senses.why: When the adjective contrasts with fiction, it certifies that the record, not the imagination, is the source.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词与虚构相对时，它确认来源是记录而非想象。

senses.title: Based on records
senses.titleCN: 基于史料的：有据可查的
senses.definition: supported by documents, evidence and scholarly sources
senses.definitionCN: 有文献、证据与学术来源支持的
senses.example: The claim is historical in the sense that two ledgers support it.
senses.exampleCN: 这一说法有史料依据，因为有两本账簿支持它。
senses.why: History is an evidence-based discipline, so the adjective can assert that documentation exists.
senses.whyCN: 历史是一门以证据为基础的学科，因此这个形容词可以断言文献确实存在。

senses.title: Studying change over time
senses.titleCN: 历时演变的：研究时间上的变化
senses.definition: in linguistics and other fields, studying a subject across its development rather than at one moment
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学等领域，研究某对象随时间的演变，而非某一时刻的状态
senses.example: Historical linguistics traces how the vowel shifted over four centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 历史语言学追踪这个元音在四百年间如何变化。
senses.why: The adjective names a method, not just a subject: the historical view compares stages of a single thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名的是方法，而不只是对象：历史的视角比较同一事物的各个阶段。

senses.title: Protected for its age
senses.titleCN: 有历史价值的：因年代而受保护
senses.definition: of a building or site, valued and often legally protected for its age and associations
senses.definitionCN: 指建筑或场所因年代与关联而受重视、常受法律保护
senses.example: The house is listed as historical and cannot be altered without permission.
senses.exampleCN: 这座房子被列为历史建筑，未经许可不得改动。
senses.why: Age becomes value when a community decides to keep a place, and the adjective carries that legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 当社区决定保留某地时，年代便成了价值，这个形容词便承载了那份法律分量。

senses.title: Original cost in accounting
senses.titleCN: 历史成本的：按取得时的价格记账
senses.definition: in accounting, valued at the price originally paid rather than at current market value
senses.definitionCN: 会计中按最初支付的价格而非当前市价计量
senses.example: The land is carried at historical cost, far below its market value.
senses.exampleCN: 这块土地按历史成本入账，远低于其市价。
senses.why: Accounting keeps the past in its books: the price at purchase is a fact about then, so the adjective marks that fixed record.
senses.whyCN: 会计把过去留在账上：购入时的价格是关于“当时”的事实，这个形容词标记的正是这一固定记录。

senses.title: Belonging to earlier times
senses.titleCN: 往昔的：属于过去而非现在
senses.definition: belonging to an earlier time and no longer current
senses.definitionCN: 属于较早时期、如今已不再通行
senses.example: Historical prices look absurdly low beside today's figures.
senses.exampleCN: 与今天的数字相比，往昔的价格低得离谱。
senses.why: The simplest reading is just 'of the past'; everything else in the word's range grows from that plain contrast with now.
senses.whyCN: 最简单的读法就是“属于过去的”；该词其余用法都从这一与“现在”的朴素对照生长出来。

intro.en: Historical is history plus -ical, from Greek historia 'inquiry' through Latin and French. It exists beside the shorter historic, with a different sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: historical 是 history 加 -ical，源自希腊 historia“探究”，经拉丁与法语传入。它与较短的 historic 并存，但含义不同。年代为约数。

items.en: historia meant 'inquiry, investigation, written account', from histōr 'witness'. The deeper origin of histōr is uncertain and often discussed.
items.cn: historia 意为“探究、调查、书面记述”，出自 histōr“见证者”。histōr 的更深来源不确定，学界多有讨论。

items.en: Latin historia covered both narrative and knowledge of events. Old French estoire gave English history in the 13th century, while story came from the same source by another route.
items.cn: 拉丁 historia 兼指叙述与对事件的了解。古法语 estoire 于 13 世纪给出英语 history，而 story 经另一路径同源而来。

items.en: English formed historic in the 17th century and historical in the 16th. For a long time they were interchangeable.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪构成 historical，17 世纪构成 historic。很长一段时间内二者可互换。

items.en: In the 18th and 19th centuries usage settled: historic means 'important in history', historical means 'relating to history or occurring in the past'.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，用法逐渐固定：historic 意为“在历史上重要的”，historical 意为“与历史有关的或发生在过去的”。

items.en: Historical linguistics, historical cost and historical record fixed the adjective in technical writing during the 19th and 20th centuries.
items.cn: 历史语言学、历史成本与历史记录在 19 至 20 世纪把该形容词固定于技术写作中。

items.en: The origin of Greek histōr is disputed, and the exact date when historic and historical stopped being interchangeable varies by source.
items.cn: 希腊 histōr 的来源有争议；historic 与 historical 不再可互换的确切年代，各家说法不一。

note.en: The first group turns on the historic/historical distinction; the second contains adjectives about the past and about records.
note.cn: 第一组聚焦 historic 与 historical 的区别；第二组是关于过去与记录的形容词。

entries.definition: Meaning 'important enough to be remembered'. A historic speech changes events; a historical speech merely happened in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“重要到值得被记住”。historic speech 改变事态；historical speech 只是发生在过去的演讲。

entries.definition: The adverb of historical. It answers 'when' or 'from what standpoint', not 'how important'.
entries.definitionCN: historical 的副词；回答“何时”或“从什么立场”，而非“多重要”。

entries.definition: A person who studies or writes history. It is a person noun, not a description of a period.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或撰写历史的人；是人物名词，不描述某个时期。

entries.definition: in a state of uncontrolled emotion, unrelated meaning
entries.definitionCN: 情绪失控的，拼写音近但意义无关

entries.definition: Relating to earlier time in general, with no implication of records or scholarship.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指较早时间，不暗示记录或学术。

entries.definition: Relating to archives and stored documents; narrower than historical, which also covers events and methods.
entries.definitionCN: 关于档案馆与所存文献；比 historical 窄，后者还覆盖事件与方法。

entries.definition: Based on or consisting of documents, or a factual film; it stresses the evidence form rather than the past itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以文献为依据或由文献构成，或指纪实影片；强调证据形式而非过去本身。

entries.definition: Handed down by custom rather than recovered from records; it describes continuity, not documentation.
entries.definitionCN: 由习俗传承而非从记录中复原；描述的是延续性，而非文献性。

entries.definition: Old and valued as an object; it applies to things, especially furniture, not to periods or methods.
entries.definitionCN: 古老而作为器物受珍视；多用于物品尤其家具，不用于时期或方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: history + -ical: belonging to history.
normal.cn: history + -ical：属于历史的。

normal.en: historical context, historical record and historical novel are the standard collocations.
normal.cn: 历史背景、历史记录、历史小说是标准搭配。

normal.en: The family is history, historical, historic, historically, historian, historiography.
normal.cn: 同族词是 history、historical、historic、historically、historian、historiography。

normal.en: historical is the neutral adjective; historic claims importance. Test with 'important': if it fits, use historic.
normal.cn: historical 是中性形容词，historic 声称重要性。可用“重要”来测：若说得通就用 historic。

normal.en: historical cost is an accounting term; do not read it as 'cost in history'.
normal.cn: historical cost 是会计术语，不要读成“历史上的成本”。

abstract.en: Picture a gloved hand turning a page of a ledger that has yellowed for two hundred years.
abstract.cn: 想象一只戴手套的手翻动一页泛黄两百年的账簿。

abstract.en: Picture a film set built from photographs, where every chair matches the year in the caption.
abstract.cn: 想象一处依据照片搭起的场景，每把椅子都与说明中的年份相符。

abstract.en: Picture the same word written in five centuries on one sheet, each hand changing the vowels.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词在五个世纪里写在同一张纸上，每一笔都改动元音。

examples.en: Historical evidence for the treaty is thin: three letters and one seal.
examples.cn: 关于这项条约的史料很单薄：三封信和一枚印章。

examples.en: The film is historical in its costumes but fictional in its plot.
examples.cn: 这部影片在服装上是历史的，情节却是虚构的。

examples.en: Historical linguistics explains why the spelling no longer matches the sound.
examples.cn: 历史语言学解释了为什么拼写不再与读音相符。

dict_mnemonic.text: “history（历史）+ ical（的）”——属于历史的 → historical 历史的、历史题材的

root: 希腊 historia“探究、记述”← histōr“见证者”；拉丁 historia、古法语 estoire → history + -ical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cluster around one idea, the recorded past, and then spread into genre, evidence, method, protection, accounting and simply 'then'.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个观念——被记录的过去——展开，随后延伸到体裁、证据、方法、保护、会计，以及朴素的“当时”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gloved hand turning a yellowed page stamped with an old seal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只戴手套的手翻动盖着旧印章的泛黄书页。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND EVIDENCE: the field and its documentary basis are the same back-and-forth.
branches.cn: 学科与证据：这门学问与其文献基础是同一套往返。

branches.en: PERIOD AND TRUTH: a setting in the past and a person who really lived both appeal to the record for authority.
branches.cn: 时期与真实：以过去为背景与确有其人，都向记录借取权威。

branches.en: METHOD: the historical view compares stages instead of freezing one moment.
branches.cn: 方法：历史的视角比较各阶段，而非冻结某一时刻。

branches.en: KEEPING THE PAST: heritage listing and historical cost both fix an earlier value into the present.
branches.cn: 留住过去：遗产登录与历史成本都把较早的价值固定进当下。

branches.en: PLAIN 'THEN': the simplest sense, from which the specialized ones branch.
branches.cn: 朴素的“当时”：最简单的义项，其余专门义项由此分支。

intro.en: Historical is history plus -ical. The Greek root historia passed through Latin and French before reaching English.
intro.cn: historical 是 history 加 -ical。希腊词根 historia 经拉丁与法语才进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The historia family in English includes history, story, historical, historic, historian and historiography; the look-alike histrionic belongs to a different Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 英语中的 historia 词族包括 history、story、historical、historic、historian、historiography；形近的 histrionic 则出自另一个拉丁词。

items.meaning: relating to history or the past
items.example: The site has historical value rather than commercial value.
items.exampleCN: 这处遗址的价值在历史而非商业。

items.meaning: the recorded past or its study
items.meaningCN: 被记录的过去或其研究
items.example: History here means the documents, not the events alone.
items.exampleCN: 这里的历史指文献，而不只是事件。

items.example: The first landing was a historic moment.
items.exampleCN: 首次登陆是一个历史性时刻。

items.example: Historically, the port handled all the grain trade.
items.exampleCN: 历史上，所有谷物贸易都由这个港口处理。

items.meaning: one who studies or writes history
items.example: The historian worked from court records.
items.exampleCN: 这位历史学家依据法庭记录工作。

items.example: Historiography asks who was left out of the record.
items.exampleCN: 史学史追问谁被排除在记录之外。

items.meaning: a narrative; a doublet of history
items.meaningCN: 叙述；history 的同源双重借词
items.example: The story and the history share one ancestor.
items.exampleCN: story 与 history 共享同一个祖先。

items.meaning: the quality of being historically real
items.example: Scholars debate the historicity of the figure.
items.exampleCN: 学者们争论这个人物是否真实存在。

latinEntries.meaning: one who knows and can testify

definition_zh: 历史；历史学；一段过往经历；病史；（事物的）沿革记录
definition_en: the study, record or remembered account of past events, especially of human affairs
core_image: 一间档案室里，纸页按年份排成长排，窗外的街景却在不断变化
scene: 考古队在城墙下挖出层叠的灶台与钱币，这些遗存让这座城的记载提前了三百年，改写本地历史。The excavation team found stacked hearths and coins beneath the city wall, remains that pushed the town's written record back three centuries and rewrote its history.
sceneCN: 这里 history 指「关于过去事件的记载与叙述」（第 1 个义项：对过往的系统记录）；句意为考古队在城墙下挖出层叠灶台与钱币，这些遗存让该城记载提前三百年，改写了本地历史。可辨识物件：层叠灶台、古钱币、城墙剖面、年份标签。

pos.zh: 历史；历史学；经历；病史（可数指一段经历或一部史书）

derivatives.zh: 历史学家
有历史意义的；历史性的
历史的；史学的
历史上；从历史角度
编史学；史学史

senses.title: The recorded past of human affairs
senses.titleCN: 对人类过往的系统记录
senses.definition: the whole body of past events as recorded, especially those of people and societies
senses.definitionCN: 被记录下来的全部过往事件，尤其是人与社会的经历
senses.example: The town's history begins with a ferry crossing and a salt tax.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城的历史始于一处渡口和一笔盐税。
senses.why: the Greek word meant inquiry, so history is first the result of asking, then the record that answers.
senses.whyCN: 希腊原词意为「探究」，因此 history 先是提问的结果，再是回答这问题的记录。

senses.title: The discipline that studies the past
senses.definition: the academic discipline that selects, checks and interprets evidence about the past
senses.definitionCN: 选择、核验并解释过去证据的学术学科
senses.example: History became a university subject with its own methods in the nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学在 19 世纪成为拥有自身方法的大学学科。
senses.why: once inquiry acquired rules of evidence and training, the word named a profession as well as a record.
senses.whyCN: 当探究有了证据规则与训练体系，这个词就既指记录，也指一门专业。

senses.title: A written narrative of events
senses.definition: a book or account that arranges past events into an ordered narrative
senses.definitionCN: 把过往事件编排为有序叙述的书或记述
senses.example: She wrote a history of the harbour that reads like a novel.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了一部读起来像小说的港口史。
senses.why: the oldest English sense was simply 'a story', and a written history is still a shaped narrative.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的义项就是「故事」，而一部史书至今仍是被塑形的叙述。

senses.title: A person's or thing's past course
senses.definition: the sequence of events that led to someone's or something's present condition
senses.definitionCN: 导致某人或某物当前状况的一系列过往事件
senses.example: The building has a history of leaks and repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼有一连串漏水和修补的经历。
senses.why: the word scales down from whole societies to a single object, because any object also has a course of events.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从整个社会缩小到单个物件，因为任何物件也都有自己的事件序列。

senses.title: A patient's medical record
senses.definition: the record of a person's past illnesses, treatments and family conditions
senses.definitionCN: 某人既往疾病、治疗与家族情况的记录
senses.example: The doctor asked about his family history of heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 医生询问他家族的心脏病史。
senses.why: medicine borrowed the word for the case narrative a doctor takes down, in the same sense of an ordered past.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用这个词指医生记下的病例叙述，仍是「有序的过去」这一层意思。

senses.title: Natural history
senses.definition: the study and record of plants, animals and minerals, including their deep past
senses.definitionCN: 对植物、动物与矿物的研究与记录，包括其深远过去
senses.example: Natural history museums preserve specimens that document extinct species.
senses.exampleCN: 自然史博物馆保存着记录已灭绝物种的标本。
senses.why: the phrase was extended from human affairs to living things once naturalists began recording change over time.
senses.whyCN: 当博物学者开始记录随时间发生的变化，这个短语便从人类事务扩展到生物。

senses.title: A track record of performance
senses.definition: the known record of how something has performed, used to judge what it will do next
senses.definitionCN: 某事物以往表现的已知记录，用以判断其下一步表现
senses.example: The fund has a history of steady returns in bad years.
senses.exampleCN: 这只基金在坏年份里有着稳定回报的往绩。
senses.why: the commercial use treats the past as evidence for the future, which is the same logic as historical inference.
senses.whyCN: 商业用法把过去当作未来的证据，这与史学推论是同一套逻辑。

senses.title: Abstract: the remembered past itself
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：被记忆的过去本身
senses.definition: the past as it is remembered, contested and used by a community in the present
senses.definitionCN: 被当下群体记忆、争夺与使用的那个过去
senses.example: The two villages tell different histories of the same flood.
senses.exampleCN: 两个村庄对同一场洪水讲述着不同的历史。
senses.why: the abstract use stresses that history is carried and argued over, not merely stored.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法强调历史是被携带、被争辩的，而不只是被存放的。

intro.en: History comes from Greek historia 'inquiry, knowledge gained by inquiry', from histor 'one who knows, witness', generally linked to idein 'to see'. It entered English through Latin and French, first meaning 'story'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: history 来自希腊 historia「探究、经由探究所得的知识」，其词源 histor 意为「知情者、见证人」，一般与 idein「看见」相联系。它经拉丁语与法语进入英语，最初意为「故事」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Histor meant 'witness, one who knows'; it is generally taken to continue a root meaning 'to see, to know', the same root behind English wit.
items.cn: histor 意为「见证人、知情者」；一般被认为延续了表示「看见、知道」的词根，英语 wit 也出于同一词根。

items.en: Historia was 'inquiry, investigation, the knowledge so gained', the word Herodotus used for his own research.
items.cn: historia 意为「探究、调查及由此获得的知识」，希罗多德就用这个词称呼自己的研究。

items.en: Latin historia kept both the inquiry and the written account, and the account sense grew stronger in later use.
items.cn: 拉丁 historia 同时保留「探究」与「成文记述」，在后世用法中记述义渐强。

items.en: Old French historie brought the word into English in the thirteenth century as 'a story, a narrative', whether true or not.
items.cn: 古法语 historie 于 13 世纪把词带入英语，意为「故事、叙述」，无论真假。

items.en: By the nineteenth century history meant the professional study of past societies, with archives, seminars and source criticism.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，history 指对过往社会的专业研究，配有档案、研讨课与史料批判。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact date when 'the past events themselves' replaced 'a story' as the dominant sense is not fixed, so the chronology given here is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：泛指「过去事件本身」取代「故事」成为主要义项的确切年代尚无定论，此处给出的时间线为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like history but name a different thing; group two holds the forms in which the past is written down.
note.cn: 第一组是外形像 history、却指别的事物的词；第二组是过去被书写下来的形态。

entries.definition: From Old French estorie, the same source as history: a narrative that may be true or invented, which is exactly what history once meant.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 estorie，与 history 同源：可真可虚构的叙述，而这正是 history 最初的义项。

entries.definition: An adjective for an event important enough to enter history, not for anything old or past.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指重要到足以载入史册的事件，而非任何古老或过去之物。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning connected with past events or with the study of them, the neutral partner of history.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为与过去事件或史学研究有关，是 history 的中性搭配词。

entries.definition: The study of how histories are written, not the events themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 研究历史如何被书写，而不是研究事件本身。

entries.definition: From Greek chronos 'time': a record arranged strictly by date, with less interpretation than a history.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 chronos「时间」：严格按日期排列的记录，解释成分少于 history。

entries.definition: The raw stored evidence, such as files and registers; history is the interpretation built on such records.
entries.definitionCN: 被保存的原始证据，如档案与登记册；history 是在这些记录之上建立的解释。

entries.definition: All that has happened; history is the part that has been selected, recorded and interpreted.
entries.definitionCN: 一切已发生之事；history 只是其中被选择、记录与解释的部分。

entries.definition: The stored documents and the place holding them; they are the raw material, not the account.
entries.definitionCN: 被保存的文件与存放它们的场所；它们是原料，不是叙述。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek historia means inquiry, so history is knowledge obtained by asking questions of evidence.
normal.cn: 希腊 historia 意为探究，所以 history 是通过追问证据获得的知识。

normal.en: Histor is the witness, one who knows, linked to the root for seeing.
normal.cn: histor 是见证人、知情者，与表示「看见」的词根相联系。

normal.en: The oldest English sense was story, which is why a history can still be told as a narrative.
normal.cn: 英语最早义项是 story，所以一部历史至今仍可作为叙述来讲。

normal.en: Keep historic and historical apart: one means momentous, the other means relating to the past.
normal.cn: 把 historic 与 historical 分开：一个指重大，一个指与过去有关。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: oral history, medical history, natural history.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分支：口述史、病史、自然史。

abstract.en: Picture shelves of paper ordered by year while the street outside keeps changing.
abstract.cn: 想象一排按年份排好的纸页，而窗外的街道不断变化。

abstract.en: Picture two villages telling the same flood in two different ways.
abstract.cn: 想象两个村庄用两种说法讲述同一场洪水。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger whose columns are evidence and whose margin is argument.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，栏目是证据，页边是争论。

examples.en: The excavation rewrote the town's history and doubled its recorded age.
examples.cn: 这次发掘改写了这座城的历史，使其有记载的年代翻了一倍。

examples.en: History is taught as a set of arguments about evidence, not as a list of dates.
examples.cn: 历史被作为一组关于证据的论证来教授，而不是一串日期。

examples.en: The fund's history of steady returns attracted cautious investors.
examples.cn: 这只基金稳定回报的往绩吸引了谨慎的投资者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「his（他的）+ story（故事）」——他的故事写成书 → 历史

root: 希腊 historia「探究、探究所得的知识」，出自 histor「见证人、知情者」，一般与 idein「看见」同根，再往上与印欧词根「看见、知道」相联系；英语 history 经拉丁 historia 与古法语 historie。更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one word from the recorded past to the discipline, the written book, a personal course, a medical file, the natural world, a track record and finally the past as memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个词展开：从被记录的过去，到学科、史书、个人经历、病历、自然界、往绩，最后是作为记忆的过去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: papers ordered by year in a room while the street outside changes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一室之内纸页按年排好，窗外街景却在变化。

branches.en: ASK AND WRITE: inquiry produces a record, and the record takes narrative shape.
branches.cn: 追问与书写：探究产生记录，记录又成为叙述。

branches.en: PROFESSION: once evidence has rules, the word names a discipline and its training.
branches.cn: 职业：证据一旦有了规则，这个词就指一门学科及其训练。

branches.en: SMALLER COURSES: a building or a fund also has a sequence that can be told and judged.
branches.cn: 更小的历程：一栋楼或一只基金同样有可被讲述与评判的序列。

branches.en: BORROWED FIELDS: medicine and natural science keep the same ordered-past logic.
branches.cn: 借用的领域：医学与自然科学保留了同一套「有序过去」逻辑。

branches.en: CONTESTED MEMORY: the past is carried and argued over, not merely shelved.
branches.cn: 被争辩的记忆：过去是被携带与争论的，不只是被束之高阁。

intro.en: History is a Greek noun in English dress; its root and endings also build historian, historic and historiography.
intro.cn: history 是披着英语外衣的希腊名词；其词根与词尾还构成 historian、historic 与 historiography。

latinIntro.en: Latin historia gives history, historian and historiography; Greek histor and the ending -ia are the building blocks.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 historia 构成 history、historian 与 historiography；希腊 histor 与词尾 -ia 是构件。

items.example: The root names the one who was there.
Historia was the title of the first prose inquiry.
items.exampleCN: historia 是第一部散文探究的标题。

items.example: history is historia in English form.
items.exampleCN: history 就是 historia 的英语形态。
那次签署具有历史意义。

items.meaning: of the past or of history

items.example: Historically, the river flooded each spring.
items.exampleCN: 历史上这条河每年春天泛滥。

items.example: Historiography studies how accounts are made.
items.exampleCN: 编史学研究所史如何被写成。

items.example: Prehistoric tools lay in the cave.

definition_en: to touch something quickly and with force, or to reach a target
core_image: 球棒与球接触的那一瞬间
scene: 棒球课上教练纠正挥棒姿势后，小选手一棒把球打出场外围栏。He swung hard and hit the incoming pitch out of the park.
sceneCN: 这里 hit 是「击打；击中」（第 1 个义项：用力快速接触）；句中挥棒正中来球，球飞出场外，正是 hit 的动作。

derivatives.zh: 现在分词，义为「击打（进行中）」
动词加名词后缀构成，义为「击球手」
复合词，义为「职业杀手」
复数名词，义为「热门作品；点击量」

senses.title: To strike with force
senses.definition: to touch someone or something quickly and with force
senses.definitionCN: 快速而用力地接触人或物
senses.example: The batsman hit the ball towards the river.
senses.exampleCN: 击球手把球朝河边打了出去。
senses.why: Speed plus force in one touch is the heart of striking.
senses.whyCN: 快速与用力一次完成，就是击打的核心。

senses.title: To crash into something
senses.definition: to crash into something with force
senses.definitionCN: 用力撞上某物
senses.example: The truck hit a tree near the bend.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在弯道附近撞上了一棵树。
senses.why: A moving body that cannot stop strikes whatever is ahead.
senses.whyCN: 停不下来的运动物体会撞上前方的任何东西。

senses.title: To reach a level or number
senses.definition: to reach a particular level, number, or price
senses.definitionCN: 达到某个数量、水平或价格
senses.example: The video hit one million views overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 视频一夜之间达到一百万播放量。
senses.why: A rising number arrives at its target like a fist at a mark.
senses.whyCN: 上升的数字像拳头一样「命中」目标刻度。

senses.title: A popular success
senses.definition: a thing, song, or show that becomes very popular
senses.definitionCN: 大受欢迎的歌曲、作品或演出
senses.example: Her first song was an instant hit online.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一首歌在网上迅速走红。
senses.why: What strikes the audience lands deep, so success is a hit.
senses.whyCN: 击中观众内心的作品，就叫 hit。

intro.en: Hit is a short native word with a violent history.
intro.cn: hit 是个简短的本族词，来历与打击相关。

items.en: Old English hittan meant to come upon or to meet by chance.
items.cn: 古英语 hittan 意为偶然遇到、碰上。

items.en: It was likely borrowed from Old Norse hitta, to hit upon or find.
items.cn: 它可能借自古诺斯语 hitta，意为碰上、找到。

items.en: The root belongs to the Germanic family of meeting and striking.
items.cn: 词根属日耳曼语族，兼有「相遇」与「击打」之意。

items.en: Middle English narrowed the sense to striking with a weapon or hand.
items.cn: 中古英语词义收窄为用手或武器击打。

items.en: Modern English added senses of reaching numbers and of popular success.
items.cn: 现代英语又添加了「达到数字」与「热门作品」之义。

note.en: Compare hit with its forms and near words.
note.cn: 把 hit 与其词形及近义词对照。

entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，双写 t
击球手，派生名词
热量，元音不同，词源无关
用力击打，常指一次重击

entries.definition: to hit a door or surface to get attention
entries.definitionCN: 敲击以引起注意
猛击并打碎，程度更强

normalIntro.en: Keep hit in motion scenes.
normalIntro.cn: 把 hit 放在运动场景中记忆。

normal.en: hit never changes: hit, hit, hit.
normal.cn: hit 的过去式、过去分词不变：hit, hit, hit。

normal.en: Only the -ing doubles the t: hitting.
normal.cn: 只有进行时分词双写 t：hitting。

normal.en: hit the road means start your journey.
normal.cn: hit the road 意为「出发上路」，与打无关。

normal.en: A hit song strikes the heart of millions.
normal.cn: hit song 击中了百万人的心——热门就是这么来的。

normal.en: Views can hit a number, like an arrow at a target.
normal.cn: 播放量能 hit 一个数字，如箭中靶。

abstract.en: Hear the sharp crack of bat on ball.
abstract.cn: 听见球棒击球的脆响——hit 的声音。

abstract.en: Feel the shock travel up your arm.
abstract.cn: 感受冲击顺着手臂传上来——hit 的触感。

abstract.en: See the number climb and touch the record line.
abstract.cn: 看见数字爬升触到纪录线——hit 的量感。

examples.en: Do not hit the dog; shout to warn it instead.
examples.cn: 别打狗，用喊声提醒它。

examples.en: The car hit the wall at the end of the street.
examples.cn: 汽车在街尾撞上了墙。

examples.en: The new phone hit the market last week.
examples.cn: 新手机上周上市了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿特」——「嘿，特准一击命中」，出手快狠正是 hit。

root: hit 大概率借自古诺斯语 hitta（碰上、找到），古英语 hittan（偶然遇到）与之呼应，属日耳曼语族；中古英语词义收窄为「击打」，现代英语再扩展出「达到」与「热门」之义。

sensesIntro.en: From a single blow to a record number to a hit song, one contact grows into many ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: hit 从一次击打延伸到「达到数值」「热门作品」，一切围绕「接触与命中」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the instant of fast, forceful contact
core.cn: 核心意象：快速而有力的接触瞬间

branches.en: a blow with hand or tool
branches.cn: 用手或工具击打（义项 01）
运动物体间的碰撞（义项 02）

branches.en: arriving at a number or level
branches.cn: 达到某个数字或水平（义项 03）

branches.en: a work that strikes the public
branches.cn: 击中大众的作品（义项 04）
力与表面的相遇（义项 01 · 02）

intro.en: Hit forms compounds about impact and success.
intro.cn: hit 构成与冲击、成功相关的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin percutere covers striking in scientific words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 percutere 在科学词汇中表示击打。

items.meaning: a player who hits the ball
items.example: She is the best hitter on the team.
items.exampleCN: 她是队里最好的击球手。

items.example: The film features a retired hitman.
items.exampleCN: 电影主角是一名退休杀手。

items.example: The page got three thousand hits.
items.exampleCN: 该页面获得三千次点击。

items.meaning: the force of one thing hitting another

items.example: Let us hit the road early.

definition_en: an activity you enjoy doing regularly in your free time
core_image: 空闲时间反复做、纯粹因为喜欢的那件事
scene: 爷爷的窗台摆满模型船，每艘都上了漆、挂了帆。Building model ships has been his hobby for thirty years.
sceneCN: 这里 hobby 是「业余爱好」（第 1 个义项：闲暇里持续喜爱的活动）；做模型船是爷爷坚持了三十年的爱好。

derivatives.zh: hobby 加 -ist 构成，义为「爱好者； hobby 的实践者」
hobby 的复数形式
近义词，义为「消遣；娱乐」

senses.title: A regular enjoyable free-time activity
senses.definition: an activity that someone enjoys doing regularly when not working
senses.definitionCN: 工作之余经常喜欢做的活动
senses.example: Her hobby is collecting stamps from old letters.
senses.exampleCN: 她的爱好是收集旧信封上的邮票。
senses.why: Free time turns into joy when a habit is repeated for pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 闲暇因重复的乐趣变成爱好。

senses.title: A small side pursuit, not a job
senses.definition: an activity followed for pleasure, not for money or a career
senses.definitionCN: 出于乐趣而非赚钱或职业的活动
senses.example: He runs a small chess club as a hobby, not a business.
senses.exampleCN: 他办了一个小棋社，纯为爱好，不为盈利。
senses.why: Money is not the aim here; the pleasure itself pays.
senses.whyCN: 这里不图钱，乐趣本身就是回报。

intro.en: Hobby has a surprising story: it grew out of a toy horse.
intro.cn: hobby 的来历出人意料：它由「玩具木马」演变而来。

items.en: Middle English hoby was a small horse or a toy horse for children.
items.cn: 中古英语 hoby 指小马或儿童玩具木马。

items.en: The word probably came through Old French hobin, a kind of horse.
items.cn: 该词可能经古法语 hobin（一种马）传入。

items.en: Riding a hobby horse meant following a favourite pastime.
items.cn: 「骑玩具马」引申为沉迷于喜欢的消遣。

items.en: By the seventeenth century, hobby meant a favourite leisure activity.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，hobby 已指喜爱的闲暇活动。

items.en: Modern English generalised it to all regular free-time pursuits.
items.cn: 现代英语把 hobby 推广到一切固定的业余活动。

note.en: Compare hobby with its family and rivals.
note.cn: 把 hobby 与词族及近义词对照。

entries.definition: a person who has a hobby
entries.definitionCN: 爱好者，派生名词
复数形式，y 变 i 加 -es
大厅；游说团体，拼写音近

entries.definition: something that fills free time pleasantly
entries.definitionCN: 消遣，指打发闲暇的乐事
兴趣，范围更广

entries.definition: an interest that takes over the mind
entries.definitionCN: 痴迷，程度过强、贬义色彩

normalIntro.en: Use the toy horse story.
normalIntro.cn: 用玩具马的故事记忆 hobby。

normal.en: hobby began as a toy horse you ride for fun.
normal.cn: hobby 最初是骑着玩的玩具木马——爱好也一样，图的就是乐。

normal.en: One hobby, many hobbies: y turns to i.
normal.cn: 一个 hobby，多个 hobbies：y 变 i 加 -es。

normal.en: hobbyist ends like artist and scientist.
normal.cn: hobbyist 的结尾与 artist、scientist 一样，都指人。

normal.en: A hobby fills the hours after school or work.
normal.cn: hobby 填满放学下班后的时光。

normal.en: Take up means start; give up means stop: take up a hobby.
normal.cn: take up 表开始：take up a hobby 即「培养一项爱好」。

abstract.en: Picture the smiling face of a wooden rocking horse.
abstract.cn: 想象摇摇木马微笑的脸——hobby 的童趣起源。

abstract.en: Feel the quiet joy of a room where you build things slowly.
abstract.cn: 感受在房间里慢慢做手工的安静喜悦——hobby 的味道。

abstract.en: See a shelf slowly filling with collected treasures.
abstract.cn: 看见架子被收藏的宝贝一点点填满。

examples.en: Photography started as a hobby and became her job.
examples.cn: 摄影起初只是爱好，后来成了她的工作。

examples.en: What hobbies do your classmates have after school?
examples.cn: 你的同学们放学后有哪些爱好？

examples.en: Gardening is a healthy hobby for old and young.
examples.cn: 园艺对老人和年轻人都是健康的爱好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「好癖」——「好（hào）癖就是喜欢的事」，hobby 是业余爱好。

root: hobby 源自中古英语 hoby（小马、玩具木马），可能经古法语 hobin 传入；「骑玩具马」引申为「沉迷消遣」，十七世纪起指业余爱好。

sensesIntro.en: Hobby means joy pursued freely, whether a quiet craft or a busy club.
sensesIntro.cn: hobby 指自由追求的乐趣：可以是安静的手工，也可以是热闹的社团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a toy horse ridden purely for delight
core.cn: 核心意象：只为快乐而骑的玩具木马

branches.en: a habit of joyful free time
branches.cn: 闲暇中固定的乐趣（义项 01）
不图回报的乐趣（义项 02）
因本身而被喜爱的业余活动（义项 01 · 02）
个人趣味的标志（义项 01）
自愿保持非职业属性（义项 02）

intro.en: Hobby joins person suffixes and time words easily.
intro.cn: hobby 易与人称后缀及时间词组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin otium means leisure in scholarly words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 otium 在学术词中表示闲暇。

items.meaning: a person devoted to a hobby
items.example: The hobbyist showed his bird photos.
items.exampleCN: 这位爱好者展示了他拍的鸟。

items.meaning: one who does it for love, not pay
items.example: An amateur painter won the prize.

items.meaning: a hobby as against one's job
